stories.title: Guinea-Bissau referendum approves new constitution that expands president's powers
stories.summary: Voters in Guinea-Bissau have approved a new constitution that significantly expands presidential powers ahead of general elections later this year. The referendum was organised by the military government that seized power in the West African nation last November following a disputed election. Voters have agreed to sweeping reforms allowing the president to appoint and dismiss the prime minister and cabinet, create or abolish ministries and dissolve parliament in the event of a grave political crisis. The main opposition party boycotted the vote, saying the process lacked adequate political and institutional safeguards and threatened the country's transition back to democracy. Guinea-Bissau, one of the poorest countries in the world, has experienced at least nine attempted and successful coups since gaining independence from Portugal in 1974. The UN has dubbed the country a "narco-state" - its coastline has many uninhabited islands, making it ideal for drug traffickers. Provisional results announced by the country's electoral commission showed that 70% of voters backed the changes in Sunday's referendum, while 30% voted against them. Turnout was reported at nearly 60%. The new constitution strengthens the presidency at the expense of the prime minister, altering the balance of power under Guinea-Bissau's semi-presidential system. Previously, Guinea-Bissau's legislature appointed a prime minister from the parliamentary majority, who then formed a cabinet - an arrangement the ruling military authorities said had contributed to political instability. The changes now give the president greater authority over the government. However, the five-year presidential term and two-term limit have been retained.

stories.title: Air China Boeing 747 grounded in New York following gate refuelling incident
stories.summary: A Boeing 747-8 operated by Air China reportedly suffered a fuel leak at New York’s John F. Kennedy International Airport early on Monday, leading to the flight being cancelled. No injuries were reported in or around the aircraft, which was expected to operate flight CA982 from New York to Beijing that day. The leak is said to have occurred between 1am and 2am while the plane was parked at the gate, according to posts on Chinese social media. It was being refuelled when the fuel truck moved away...

stories.title: Upper Thailand faces heavy rain, flood risk until Sept 7
stories.summary: The Thai Meteorological Department (TMD) has warned of isolated heavy to very heavy rain across upper Thailand from Sept 4 to Sept 7, raising the risk of flash floods and run-off. The advisory, issued at 5am on Sept 2, warned that northern and north-eastern Thailand are expected to experience the heaviest rainfall. The department attributed the conditions to a monsoon trough extending across the north and upper north-east, combined with a moderate south-west monsoon prevailing over the Andaman Sea, Thailand and the Gulf of Thailand. The advisory did not identify individual provinces, specifying only the north and north-east as the areas of greatest concern. TMD warned that heavy and accumulated rainfall could cause flash floods, rapid run-off and short-term inundation. Tropical Storm Saudel, located over the upper South China Sea, is forecast to move close to Taiwan between Sept 5 and Sept 7.
